studies.headline_metric: 36/5,400 pre-fix vs. 0/10,800 post-fix overspends · tight-budget gain did not replicate (reported_j)
studies.headline_claim: Moving goal comparison and receipt bookkeeping inside the budget guard cut episode overspends from 36/5,400 in exploratory Run 1 (firing falsifier R-F2) to 0/10,800 in preregistered Run 2 (Darwin ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j), while the exploratory +2.65 tight-budget Sudoku task gain at B = 1.0 failed to replicate and falsifiers R-F1 through R-F6 fired.
plain_bullets: An agent must aim at a goal, act on the world, and stay within an energy budget.
Physics prices every decision, creating one optimal pace between slow idle drain and frantic switching waste.
Among systems that finish a task correctly, the smarter one is whichever spent less energy.
studies.methods_and_meter: Apple Silicon macOS proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj (L3 reported_j) and x86-64 Linux powercap RAPL (L2 reported_j) plus calibrated cycle accounting across 30 Sudoku constraint tasks and N = 10,800 preregistered episodes (40 seeds x 3 arms x 3 budgets). No external DC shunt or wall analyzer was attached (measured_j = null).
studies.baseline_comparison: Compares adaptive cascade routing against a fixed heuristic cascade and a goal-blind unguarded loop. External LLM or commercial SAT/CSP solver baselines were not benchmarked in this study.
studies.limitations_and_scope: Six falsifiers fired: R-F1 (guard overhead on tiny acts), R-F2 (pre-fix overspends), R-F3/replication check (tight-budget B = 1.0 gain failed to replicate; only loose B = 2.0 closure +2.8 tasks held), R-F4 (cross-machine rank reversal Kendall tau-b = -0.037), R-F5 (CV > 0.25 on unquiesced hosts), and R-F6 (integrated derivative mismatch). Sub-millisecond 0.04 ms acts also aliased ~1 ms Linux RAPL updates (320-327 overspends in Machine 2 Part A).
studies.skeptic_question: Earlier summaries sounded like sweeping thermodynamic slogans—yet your own preregistered Run 2 failed to replicate the tight-budget Sudoku gain and fired six falsifiers. What actually survived replication?
studies.architect_answer: That critique is spot on. Modern CPUs run 14 to 15 orders of magnitude above k_B T ln 2, so physics bounds only enforce sign positivity. What survived preregistered Run 2 across 10,800 episodes is the guard-boundary engineering lesson: billing comparison and receipt overhead before committing an act cut overspends from 36 in 5,400 down to 0 in 10,800, while exposing ~1 millisecond Linux RAPL counter aliasing on sub-millisecond steps.
studies.skeptic_followup: And what about the adaptive controller beating the fixed cascade when energy is tight?
studies.architect_rebuttal: At tight budget B = 1.0, that +2.65 task edge vanished in preregistered Run 2 and cross-machine rankings reversed with Kendall tau-b = -0.037. Only loose-budget B = 2.0 closure replicated, so we report the negative replication openly under Signed Provenance · Self-Checked.

studies.title: Metered Commit Gates: KV260 Whole-SOM Shunt Readings, Statistical Bounds, and Cascade Scope

studies.headline_claim: Whole-module VCC_SOM TI INA260 halt-vs-run power-slope readings on an AMD Kria KV260 board recorded 11,428 pJ/cycle (11.43 nJ, SE = 129 pJ across N = 4 interleaved 25 s passes at 25 MHz, measured_j), while a 98.0 pJ seed-fabric delta remained inconclusive near the 1.25 mA INA260 current step; software pendulum checks observed 0 false allows in 209,261 trials (95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound <= 1.43e-5).
plain_bullets: A computer should not take an irreversible action until an independent check confirms it is safe.
It should try the cheapest method first and wake a large AI model only when simpler tools miss.
Every decision is written to a receipt with the energy it used, so anyone can audit it later.
studies.methods_and_meter: Hardware rung: AMD Kria KV260 onboard TI INA260 DC shunt on VCC_SOM (5.04 V whole-SOM rail including ARM PS, UltraScale+ PL, DDR4, and regulators; N = 4 A/B/A 25 s windows at ~4 Hz, ~6.25e8 8-lane cycles/window, measured_j). Software cascade rungs use analytical/simulated models (est_j / [M]), never mixed with measured_j.
studies.baseline_comparison: Hardware compares halted-clock vs 25 MHz 8-lane gate stepping on the same KV260 module (+0.2857 W, SE = 0.0032 W). Software compares Lyapunov Vdot and Control Barrier Function gates against unguarded actuation and stationary Zipf(s = 1.1) vs cold arrival streams.
studies.limitations_and_scope: The 11.43 nJ/cycle reading is whole-SOM module power, not isolated transistor energy, and the 98 pJ (+1.96 mA) seed delta is explicitly inconclusive near the 1.25 mA ADC step. In NI-4, port-Hamiltonian and CBF safety predicates disagreed on boundary states, showing a gate enforces only its encoded predicate. The 16.7x Mixture-of-Limits frontier call cut assumes stationary Zipf(1.1) repeats and drops to 1.0x on all-novel cold arrivals.
studies.skeptic_question: You quote 11,428 picojoules per gate cycle on KV260 and zero false allows—isn’t VCC_SOM measuring the entire system-on-module, and doesn’t finite simulation stop short of universal safety?
studies.architect_answer: Exactly right on both counts. VCC_SOM feeds the Cortex-A53 subsystem, DDR4, regulators, and FPGA fabric together, giving 11.43 nanojoules per 8-lane cycle across 4 interleaved 25-second halt-versus-run passes, while the 98 picojoule seed delta sits right near the 1.25 milliamp INA260 step and is marked inconclusive. Likewise, 0 false allows in 209,261 pendulum states sets a 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound of 1.43e-5 under that generator—not universal bug absence.
studies.skeptic_followup: What happens when two mathematically reasonable safety gates inspect the exact same state?
studies.architect_rebuttal: Experiment NI-4 tested exactly that: a port-Hamiltonian passivity gate and a Control Barrier Function gate disagreed on boundary excursions. A commit gate guarantees conformance to its written predicate, never generic physical safety beyond the specification.

In known physics, no quantum trick, analog circuit, or reported anomaly sends readable answers backward in time.
Every fast lookup of a future answer is work paid upfront, which fresh random values defeat immediately.

studies.architect_rebuttal: Zero hardware energy was measured—its class is strictly unmetered. And a 2^16 FFT is purely a finite-sample linear periodicity control, never a substitute for differential or algebraic cryptanalysis.

Cheaper computer work still inspires people to start many more jobs, so total use keeps rising.
Money prices for AI are falling fast, but the physical electricity it burns is never free.

studies.headline_claim: Packs 256 six-input LUT6 gates plus a 672 B zero-MUL ternary T-MAC tail into a 4,096 B #![no_std] Rust CompactLut6Page, stating upfront that 2^6 = 64 and 4^3 = 64 is strictly a combinatorial counting parallel used for naming—NOT a biophysical isomorphism; separates Jetson AGX Thor TI INA3221 shunts (162.56 nJ/op bit-sliced, 1,935.05 nJ scalar, measured_j), live Alif Cortex-M55 DWT cycles (684.6 cycles), and Numato Aller A7 XC7A200T openXC7 320.62 MHz gateware estimates (0.86 est_W, 55.2 est_C with DDR3 off vs 95.8 est_C bare thermal failure with DDR3 on, est_j).
plain_bullets: Living cells use sixty-four genetic triplets to store survival rules, and digital six-input lookup tables use the exact same sixty-four switches.
Grouping four neighboring switch settings together absorbs small sensor or wording glitches while eliminating brittle high-frequency noise.
A sixteen-kilobyte core runs verified skills in nanoseconds from four-dollar microcontrollers to fanless M.2 circuit cards, waking large models only on genuine novelty.
studies.methods_and_meter: Strictly separated substrates: (1) Jetson AGX Thor TI INA3221 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS shunt (measured_j); (2) M5 Max / Zen 5 counters (reported_j); (3) USB-attached OpenMV-AE3 Alif Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz DWT cycle counter (unmetered); and (4) Artix-7 XC7A200T Verilator 12,023-cycle co-sim + openXC7 post-PAR .bit + DS181/UG475 thermal/leakage model (est_j / est_C).
studies.baseline_comparison: Compares CompactLut6Page + Antisym-40 T-MAC against INT8/BF16 Micro-MLPs (87.00x Thor CpJ; 0.0000% silent corruption at 1% SEU bit-flip injection with (72,64) SECDED vs 54.56% INT8 MLP) and DDR3-active vs DDR3-reset M.2 gateware.
studies.limitations_and_scope: Biological terms (codon, wobble, operon, apoptosis) are purely naming mnemonics for a 4 KB binary page—what NucleusCodon.lean machine-checks is standard Boolean Walsh-Hadamard degree-5/6 cancellation (Linial, Mansour & Nisan 1993). Physical M.2 +3.3 V Kelvin shunt (INA228) and thermocouple probing on XC7A200T have not yet been run (LA-F30), and bare 0-LFM operation with DDR3 enabled exceeds 85 C (95.8 est_C thermal failure).
studies.skeptic_question: Be honest: calling 64-bit LUT6 tables "codons" and "wobble bases" because 2^6 and 4^3 both equal 64—is that biology or Boolean algebra, and did you probe the M.2 FPGA rails?
studies.architect_answer: It is 100% Boolean algebra—2^6 = 64 and 4^3 = 64 is strictly a naming mnemonic for the 4-kilobyte binary page layout, not a biological isomorphism! What NucleusCodon.lean machine-checks across 6 Lean kernels is classical Linial-Mansour-Nisan Walsh-Hadamard Fourier cancellation: subcube-invariant 2-bit masks zero out degree-5 and degree-6 high-frequency noise. And on hardware, Jetson Thor 162.56 nanojoules per op is physical INA3221 measured_j, whereas the Artix-7 M.2 card is openXC7 320.62 MHz post-PAR est_j—which candidly flags a 95.8 Celsius thermal failure in a bare 0-LFM slot unless DDR3 is held in reset!
studies.skeptic_followup: How does it behave on bare-metal microcontrollers without floating-point units?
studies.architect_rebuttal: The #![no_std] Rust crate compiles with zero float instructions into 25% of 64 KB SRAM on Cortex-M4F and RV32IMAC, and ran in 684.6 DWT cycles—1.72 microseconds, 173.8x faster than INT8 Micro-MLP—on a live USB-attached Alif Cortex-M55.
